nodes.text: Humane institutions can survive and spread while retaining autonomy and care, within ecological limits and without catastrophic destruction.
nodes.label: Humane institutions survive and spread while retaining autonomy and care within liveable limits.

nodes.text: Communities can maintain useful material and organisational capabilities at viable cost.
nodes.label: Communities maintain useful capabilities at viable cost.

nodes.text: Members retain substantive control, justified trust and meaningful freedom to disagree or leave.
nodes.label: Members retain control, justified trust and freedom to disagree or leave.

nodes.text: Ecological and catastrophic risks remain compatible with continued human life and collective agency.
nodes.label: Ecological and catastrophic risks remain compatible with continued human agency.

backlog.label: Check this proposed common ground with the people in the discussion.
backlog.note: The supplied analyses report apparent agreements. None is recorded here as accepted; compare the original posts before inviting participants to review the wording.

backlog.label: Define realised progress, including survival and retention of the mission.
backlog.note: The first analysis proposes adoption retained in practice, with viability and faithfulness measured separately. Agree a bounded system, period and observable outcome rather than equating publications, satisfaction or market growth with success.

backlog.label: Review the wider programme before choosing further branches.
backlog.note: The second analysis also covers reflective development, the Laboratory, Forge/model adaptation, Vocal Presence, federation, material and energy services, and enforceable security. Its spiritual root is a philosophical hypothesis. This compact map does not establish a single global constraint or make the pilot the whole programme.

nodes.text: As a group grows, damaging disagreements can exceed members’ current conflict-handling capacity.

assumptions.text: Conflict-handling capacity is insufficient for the selected function, and effective member-controlled alternatives are not already available.

backlog.label: Test whether conflict capacity limits this particular group's next achievement.
backlog.note: Compare developmental capacity, coordination design, resources and external pressures. A reported historical mechanism is not a measured constraint at a selected host.

backlog.note: Retain non-AI and optional-AI comparators. The stronger claim is reported in the analyses, not attributed here as a verified commitment by Leif or Robert.

backlog.label: Compare AI guidance with optional-AI and human approaches.
backlog.note: Check useful output, total cost, energy, member control, fallback and competence without the tool. Participants have not committed to running this comparison.

backlog.label: Decide in advance what evidence would change the hypothesis.
backlog.note: Lower satisfaction scores or fewer complaints alone do not establish benefit. The first analysis asks whether small democratic groups gain more than hierarchies; the second distinguishes local improvements from the still-unclosed institutional-selection claim F17. One successful pilot cannot establish the larger claim.

backlog.label: Assess suppressed grievances separately from satisfaction.
backlog.note: Retain independent human support and a way to report costs, unfairness, dependency and increased concentration of authority.

backlog.label: Verify the actual host's obstacles rather than assuming missing details are missing capacity.
backlog.note: The PDF distinguishes documented gaps, source-defined risks, reconstructed requirements and conditions to check locally (D/S/R/X). This statement concerns evidence in the supplied record, not proof that no willing host or resources exist.

backlog.label: Agree measures, responsibilities, resources and a person who can assess the outcomes.
backlog.note: No owner, budget, baseline, target, date or feedback commitment is assigned here. A trial is not ready until the affected people confirm these conditions. Future benefit and harm feedback should preserve both original expectations.

backlog.note: This is a proposed action, not an invitation already sent or a commitment by Leif, Robert or any cooperative.

history.title: First source reconstruction
history.summary: A compact map prepared from two supplied analyses. Every statement and connection is proposed; no participant endorsement, assigned trial owner or observed outcome is recorded.

changes.note: Selected and paraphrased by the AI from the supplied analyses. Review the sources and assumptions before relying on the map.

sources.title: Second Renaissance Causal and Prerequisite Trees · version 2 · 22 October 2026
sources.description: Supplied 48-page analysis. Page numbers and identifiers on each item refer to this document. It reconstructs an expanded forum discussion (posts 1–36) and five documents attributed to Leif Eriksson: Bindings and the Captive Mind; The Last Shall Be First; The Countercurrent’s Paradox of Success; Where Is the Deepest Leverage Point; and The Carbon Pulse. These primary sources were not supplied separately or independently checked here. A locator is an audit trail into the supplied analysis, not verification of the original claim or the participants’ agreement.

sources.title: Second Renaissance thread: thinking-process trees · supplied text · 22 October 2026
sources.description: Supplied earlier analysis and presentation notes, based on a reported 32-post forum thread. Its throughput and governance-capacity proposals are hypotheses for a bounded case. The later PDF broadens the programme and distinguishes local improvements from a durable change in institutional selection. The draft introductory forum post was not sent. No original forum URL or manuscript excerpt is published as if independently verified.
